You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From fe6653460ee7a7dbe0cd5fd322992af862ce5ab0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Pan Bian <bianpan2016@163.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Jan 2021 01:18:47 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] mtd: spi-nor: hisi-sfc: Put child node np on error path

Put the child node np when it fails to get or register device.

Fixes: e523f11141bd ("mtd: spi-nor: add hisilicon spi-nor flash controller driver")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Pan Bian <bianpan2016@163.com>
[ta: Add Fixes tag and Cc stable]
Signed-off-by: Tudor Ambarus <tudor.ambarus@microchip.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20210121091847.85362-1-bianpan2016@163.com
---
 drivers/mtd/spi-nor/controllers/hisi-sfc.c | 4 +++-
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/controllers/hisi-sfc.c b/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/controllers/hisi-sfc.c
index 7c26f8f565cb..47fbf1d1e557 100644
--- a/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/controllers/hisi-sfc.c
+++ b/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/controllers/hisi-sfc.c
@@ -399,8 +399,10 @@ static int hisi_spi_nor_register_all(struct hifmc_host *host)
 
 	for_each_available_child_of_node(dev->of_node, np) {
 		ret = hisi_spi_nor_register(np, host);
-		if (ret)
+		if (ret) {
+			of_node_put(np);
 			goto fail;
+		}
 
 		if (host->num_chip == HIFMC_MAX_CHIP_NUM) {
 			dev_warn(dev, "Flash device number exceeds the maximum chipselect number\n");
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by a failure to properly release the reference to the child device node (`np`) when the registration of the SPI NOR flash device failed. This could lead to a memory leak, as the reference to the node would not be decremented, preventing the memory associated with it from being freed. The patch corrects this by adding a call to `of_node_put(np)` in the error handling path, ensuring that the reference is released when an error occurs during device registration.

You are a programming expert.
    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by a failure to properly release the reference to the child device node (`np`) when the registration of the SPI NOR flash device failed. This could lead to a memory leak, as the reference to the node would not be decremented, preventing the memory associated with it from being freed. The patch corrects this by adding a call to `of_node_put(np)` in the error handling path, ensuring that the reference is released when an error occurs during device registration.
